subject.title: [Bug]: 2 codex accounts, same machine, same docs, one has balloon startup cost

question: Should local Codex stdio app-server state remain per-agent, or move to per-auth-profile with explicit reset, migration, cleanup, and docs behavior for existing `codex-home` state?
rationale: The source-backed fix direction changes a persisted native Codex state boundary that includes auth, config, sessions, SQLite/logs, plugins, and caches, so automation should not choose the upgrade semantics by itself.

options.title: Profile-scope Codex homes with explicit upgrade behavior
options.body: Move profile-backed stdio launches under per-auth-profile Codex homes, document whether existing state is migrated or intentionally reset, and require redacted two-account proof before closing.

options.title: Keep per-agent homes and diagnose another root cause
options.body: Leave the storage boundary unchanged until a live repro proves the cached prefix comes from shared `CODEX_HOME` rather than another Codex account or hosted cache behavior.

options.title: Document same-agent account switching as unsupported
options.body: Treat multiple OAuth accounts in one OpenClaw agent as unsupported and direct users to separate agents or configs instead of changing the default state layout.

recommendation.title: Profile-scope Codex homes with explicit upgrade behavior
recommendation.body: Move profile-backed stdio launches under per-auth-profile Codex homes, document whether existing state is migrated or intentionally reset, and require redacted two-account proof before closing.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete landed the central Codex OAuth ownership work and has adjacent follow-up history in the same bridge/runtime surface.
